title: Region-aware WORM visibility & automated evidence bundles for admin audit trails
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a production-grade pipeline that records admin actions (role changes, policy edits, access grants), configuration mutations, and elevated access sessions into region-tagged WORM storage and emits verifiable evidence bundles for automated reporting and regulatory queries. The goal is end-to-end tamper-evident retention with fast verification surface (signed manifests), residency-aware retention enforcement, and a nightly reporting job that assembles and ships attestations to legal/compliance teams.
acceptance_criteria: All admin actions are written to append-only storage with retention-lock/enforced immutability for configured retention windows per-region.
Each retention period and residency policy is reflected via a signed manifest (sealed-object manifest) that contains object digests, region tag, retention expiry, and an RFC-3161 timestamp signature.

Evidence bundles for a given day/region can be produced automatically and contain: manifest.json (signed), index.csv (human-readable), a sha256 manifest root, and an audit-report.pdf generated from the manifest. Bundles are archived to an escrow bucket and a custody record is created in the compliance dashboard.
Verification flow for reviewers: given a bundle URL, the compliance UI can validate signatures, check retention locks, and optionally perform object spot-checks without downloading full payloads.
Cross-region replication respects residency: objects tagged for EU stay in EU buckets; replication for resiliency uses region-pairing allowed by policy and preserves lock semantics.
Automated daily report job runs with alerting on failure and exports an evidence summary to Confluence and Slack #compliance-alerts channel.
implementation_steps: Design data model for sealed-object manifest (digest list, region, retention_expiry, object_keys, producer_id, timestamp).
Prototype using S3 Object Lock (governance mode) and Azure immutable blobs in parallel on a small sample of admin events. Measure latency and storage costs.
Implement a manifest signer service that uses HSM-backed keys (KMS/HSM integration) to produce RFC-3161 compatible timestamps and signatures.
Build residency reconciler: background job that verifies objects for a region do not have cross-region residency flags and rehydrates or quarantines violations.
Create evidence bundler that zips manifest + index + audit report and pushes to escrow bucket and registers custody record in console API.
Add console UI hooks: evidence download, signature verification UI, and a read-only preview of index.csv for quick triage.
End-to-end tests and infra-as-code: CloudFormation/Terraform modules to provision immutable buckets with retention policies and write-only service accounts.
Operational runbook: incident steps for unlocked object remediation, manifest re-issuance, and legal hold extensions.
Security review and penetration test for signer service and S3 presign flow.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: S3 Object Lock semantics differ across clouds (Azure/ GCP). Mitigation: implement abstraction layer and store canonical manifest in our ledger service to unify verification.
Risk: Long retention windows increase storage and cost. Mitigation: tiered lifecycle + cold-storage exports with searchable manifests retained hot for quick verification.
Risk: HSM key rotation could invalidate prior signatures if done incorrectly. Mitigation: maintain a key-version registry and sign manifest with key metadata so past signatures remain verifiable.
Risk: Cross-region DR vs residency rules conflict. Mitigation: residency reconciler and policy-driven authorized replica pairs documented in compliance policy.
decisions: Use signed sealed-object manifests as the canonical verification surface rather than direct object downloads to allow fast spot-checks.
Primary immutable storage: cloud provider native Object Lock / Immutable Blob; secondary canonical ledger stored in an internal append-only database with HSM-stamped roots.
Adopt RFC-3161 timestamping service backed by internal HSM; optionally anchor daily root hash to an external public ledger if required by customer audits.
Evidence bundles will be retained for 7 years by default (configurable per-customer) and stored in an escrow container with stricter access roles.
notes: Prototype results (2026-03-05): S3 Object Lock governance mode writes add ~25ms median to ingest path; Azure immutable blob add ~40ms in our test harness.
Cost estimate: incremental storage + escrow ~ +4.3% for standard workloads with 1-year retention; longer retention increases percent impact.
Operational note: legal-hold API must be able to extend retention without requiring object mutation; use metadata-driven extension and a separate hold registry.
